title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

As we approach the final trading day of 2025, markets remain in a consolidation phase. The major indices are in a mixed technical state, with large-cap indices holding up relatively better than their mid- and small-cap counterparts. The mid-cap index has slipped below its 10-day moving average, while the small-cap index has fallen below both its 10- and 20-day moving averages. Despite this short-term weakness, all major indices remain in intermediate-term uptrends above rising 50-day moving averages, indicating that the broader trend remains intact as the market works through a corrective phase.

Market internals reflect this same mixed backdrop. Large-cap stocks continue to show relative resilience, with pockets of new highs and modest upside momentum. In contrast, mid- and small-cap stocks are weaker beneath the surface, with new lows outpacing new highs and downside momentum expanding. This divergence in internal strength highlights the market’s lack of upside conviction and helps explain the ongoing scarcity of clean, actionable setups.

Sector action remains similarly uneven. Financials, Healthcare, and Materials continue to lead on both relative performance and trend, offering the most constructive opportunities. Meanwhile, Industrials, Technology, and Consumer sectors are still struggling to regain momentum and establish a firm technical footing. Other areas—such as Energy, Defensives, Utilities, and Real Estate—appear to be forming short-term bottoms, but continue to lag in overall price performance and remain lower-priority until strength improves.

Overall, the market remains in a holding pattern: intermediate-term trends are intact, but short-term conditions remain corrective and selective. Patience and discipline remain essential as the market works through this consolidation and waits for clearer direction.

Overall Trend: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Mixed

  • Small Cap: Negative

Overall NH/NL Breadth: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Negative

  • Small Cap: Negative

Overall Up/Down Momentum: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Negative

  • Small Cap: Negative

Market Recap

Market Monitor (Click Here)

1. Trend & Market Structure

The market remains in an intermediate-term uptrend, but is working through a short-term corrective phase.

  • All major indices remain above rising 50-day moving averages, preserving the intermediate trend.

  • Large caps are holding up relatively better.

  • Mid caps have slipped below the 10-day MA.

  • Small caps are weaker, now below both the 10- and 20-day MAs.

Tactical Guidance

  • Maintain a neutral-to-light long bias.

  • Avoid increasing exposure until:

    • Mid and small caps stabilize and reclaim short-term MAs, or

    • Large caps break decisively higher out of consolidation.

  • Respect the 50-day MA as the key line in the sand for trend integrity.

  • A failure of the 50-day on multiple indices would warrant a more defensive posture.

2. Breadth & Momentum Monitoring

Internals are mixed and reflect uneven participation.

  • Large-cap stocks show relative resilience with pockets of new highs and improving momentum.

  • Mid- and small-cap stocks remain internally weak, with:

    • New lows exceeding new highs

    • Expanding downside momentum

This divergence reflects limited conviction and selective buying pressure.

Tactical Guidance

  • Treat internals as neutral-to-cautious.

  • Require confirmation before increasing risk:

    • Contracting new lows

    • Expansion of new highs beyond large caps

  • Until participation broadens, assume breakouts may be less reliable.

3. Sector Allocation & Focus

Sector leadership remains narrow and rotational.

Primary Focus (Best Relative Strength & Trend)

  • Financials

  • Healthcare

  • Materials

These sectors continue to offer the most constructive combination of trend and relative performance.

Secondary / Watching for Improvement

  • Industrials

  • Technology

  • Consumer

These groups are still working to regain footing and are lower priority until relative strength improves.

Lagging / Avoid for Now

  • Energy

  • Defensives

  • Utilities

  • Real Estate

While some are forming short-term bottoms, they continue to lag in performance and lack confirmation.

Tactical Guidance

  • Concentrate exposure in leading sectors only.

  • Avoid spreading capital across rotational or lagging groups.

4. Stock Selection & Trade Execution

Opportunity remains limited and selective.

Preferred Setups

  • Tight consolidations near rising 20- or 50-day MAs

  • Stocks holding structure during market consolidation

  • Relative strength leaders within Financials, Healthcare, and Materials

Avoid

  • Extended names

  • Early breakout attempts without volume

  • Stocks below key moving averages, especially in weak sectors

Execution Rules

  • Use ½ to ⅔ normal position size.

  • Be patient—let setups come to you.

  • If actionable setups are scarce, staying mostly in cash is appropriate.

5. Risk & Position Management

Capital preservation remains a priority in this environment.

  • Exposure: Moderate (45–60%)

  • Cash: Maintain 30–40% for flexibility

  • Stops: Below recent swing lows or the 20-day MA

  • Trim positions that stall or lose relative strength.

6. Scenario Planning

Bullish Resolution

  • Large caps break higher

  • Mid/small caps reclaim short-term MAs

  • Breadth improves across market caps

→ Gradually increase exposure toward 65–75%.

Continued Consolidation

  • Indices remain range-bound

  • Internals stay mixed

→ Maintain selective exposure and avoid overtrading.

Breakdown

  • Multiple indices lose the 50-day MA

  • New lows expand further

→ Reduce exposure toward 30–40% and prioritize defense.

Bottom Line

The market is digesting gains into year-end, with intermediate trends intact but short-term conditions still corrective and selective. Leadership is narrow, internals are mixed, and clean setups remain scarce. This is an environment for patience, discipline, and selective positioning, not aggressive risk-taking. Let participation broaden and conviction return before leaning more heavily into the long side.
